connector: Last week Jemmy went back for the prince, and they rode off in Captain Nips’ potato coach. Today the coach is stopped on the river road. Jemmy hides. Watch what the prince says when the outlaws ask where the whipping boy went.

a.raw: run now the prince ordered i wont wait for you
a.fixed: “Run now!” the prince ordered. “I won’t wait for you!”
a.why: Each thing the prince says gets its own quotation marks. Run and I start new sentences, so they get capitals. Won’t needs an apostrophe. The exclamation marks go inside the closing quotation marks.

b.raw: stop the coach jemmy shouted we left him behind
b.fixed: “Stop the coach!” Jemmy shouted. “We left him behind!”
b.why: Each thing Jemmy says gets its own quotation marks. Stop, Jemmy, and We get capitals. The exclamation marks go inside the closing quotation marks.

mfill1.h1: Say re, then build. Push them together with no space.
mfill1.why: re + build = rebuild: to build again.

mfill2.h1: Say un, then happy. Push them together.

mfill3.h1: Say pre, then view. Push them together.
mfill3.why: pre + view = preview: to view before.

mfill4.h1: Say dis, then agree. Push them together.
mfill4.why: dis + agree = disagree: to not agree.

mfill5.h1: Say mis, then read. Push them together.
mfill5.why: mis + read = misread: to read wrong.

match.pluck: Jemmy sees a cast-iron streak of it in the prince. Look for the meaning about courage.
match.defiant: Defiant is about standing firm. Look for the meaning about refusing to give in.
match.girded: The prince girded himself for the next blow. Look for the meaning about getting ready.
match.snarling: Snarling is a sound. Look for the meaning about a growl.

items.title: Front word parts
items.q: Betsy slipped the rope back around the bear’s neck. She had to retie it. What does retie mean?
items.why: re means again. Retie means tie again.

miss.1: That would be untie. Look for the meaning with again.

items.title: Front word parts
items.q: The river road was unsafe with outlaws about. What does unsafe mean?
items.why: un means not. Unsafe means not safe.

miss.0: Before would be pre. Which word part is at the front of unsafe?

items.title: Front word parts
items.q: A sign that points the wrong way can mislead you. What does mislead mean?
items.why: mis means wrong. Mislead means lead the wrong way.

miss.0: Again would be re. Which word part is at the front of mislead?

items.title: Sound-alike words
items.q: Captain Nips had ___ horses pulling his coach.

miss.1: too means also or more than enough. Here you need a number.

items.title: Sound-alike words
items.q: The prince was whipped, and Jemmy was hurt ___. Which word means also?
items.why: too, with two o’s, can mean also.

miss.0: to points somewhere. Here you need the word that means also.

items.title: Sound-alike words
items.why: to points somewhere: to the river.

miss.1: two is a number. Billy ran toward a place.

items.title: Prepositional phrases
items.q: Cutwater ran off like a greyhound. What does like a greyhound tell you?
items.why: like a greyhound tells how he ran: very fast.

miss.1: A greyhound is not a place. It tells the way he ran.

items.title: Prepositional phrases
items.q: The rooster crowed before dawn. What does before dawn tell you?
items.why: Dawn is a time. Before dawn tells when.

miss.0: It is not the way the rooster crowed. Dawn is a time.

glossary.m: a boy kept in the castle to be punished whenever the prince does something wrong
the big lesson a story teaches. You can say it in one sentence.
a word part at the front of a word that changes its meaning, like re in rebuild
words that sound the same but mean different things and are spelled differently, like to, two, and too
a group of words that starts with a preposition and ends on a noun, like under the straw
writing about a thing as if it were a person, like a sea that crawls
the last sentence of a paragraph. It says your big idea in a new way.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Last week Jemmy went back for the prince. Now they’re riding in a coach full of potatoes, and somebody shouts, Stand and deliver! The outlaws are back. Today, watch the prince closely. He does something Jemmy never expected.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first. You’ll meet five word parts that go at the front of a word. Then you’ll sort phrases that tell where, when, or how, and spell three words that sound exactly the same.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: Jemmy hides in Chapter 16, and the outlaws grab the prince. Watch what the prince says, and watch what he does not do. Then in Chapter 17, someone comes to help.
transcripts.guide3: This week you compare Jemmy and the prince. Today, fill in the chart for each boy: how he started, how he ends, and what changed him.

notes.wordParts: These word parts go at the front of a word. re = again (rebuild), un = not (unhappy), pre = before (preview), dis = not (disagree), mis = wrong (misread).
notes.grammar: A prepositional phrase starts with a preposition and ends on a noun: through the fog. It can tell where, when, or how.
notes.spelling: Homophones sound the same but mean different things. to points (to the gate), two is the number 2, too means also or more than enough. their = belongs to them, there = a place, they’re = they are.
notes.wgrd: In the last chapters of a book, good readers start to see its lesson. That lesson is called the theme.
vocab: courage; being brave when things are hard

The exclamation marks go inside. Tap the yellow parts to see each rule. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Think about the question. Tap See what was hiding. Then type each whole word and tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's a trick for big words. Cover the front part. Retell. Cover the re, and tell is left. Re means again, so retell means tell again. Five word parts work like that. Re means again. Pre means before. Mis means wrong. And two of them mean not: un and dis. Read the five words, and think about the question. Then tap See what was hiding. Last, type each whole word.

mods.todo: Listen to each card. Guess the meaning, then flip the card. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Let's be word detectives. In Chapter 17, Jemmy watches the prince get up off the mud, and he thinks: There was a cast-iron streak of pluck in him. Cast iron is hard and strong. So pluck must be something strong inside a person. Courage! Now tap Opti reads it on each card. Guess, then flip. Then play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each phrase: where, when, or how.
mods.script: Listen. Jemmy hid. Jemmy hid under the potatoes. The new part starts with under and ends with potatoes. That whole group is a prepositional phrase. It starts with a preposition and ends on a noun. Some tell where, like under the potatoes. Some tell when, like after dark. Some tell how, like with a shout. Tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each phrase: where, when, or how.

mods.todo: Read the three sentences. Tap See the Rule. Then sort each phrase: to, two, or too.
mods.script: Say these with me. To. Two. Too. They sound exactly the same! Your ears can't help you, so the spelling has to. Two, t w o, is the number, like two boys. Too, with two o's, means also, or more than enough, like too hot. To points somewhere, like to the castle. Read the three sentences, and tap See the Rule. Then tap each phrase, and tap the spelling it needs.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.todo: Write the sentence three new ways, one box at a time.
mods.script: [warmly] Remember copia? It means saying one idea in many ways. Watch me try one first, with a different sentence. The coach stopped. Box one, change the opener: On the river road, the coach stopped. Box two, swap the verb for a stronger one: The coach jolted to a halt. Box three, add a detail: The old potato coach stopped. Now it's your turn, one box at a time. If you get stuck, tap Show one way.

Here's something to think about. Jemmy tells the prince to say he swam the river. Then he hides, and he holds his breath. He thinks the prince might give him away again, like he did in Chapter 12. Will he? Keep that question with you while you read.

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read Ch. 16–17 in your book.
mods.script: Time to read Chapters 16 and 17. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. In Chapter 16, the outlaws stop the coach, and Billy picks up a whip. Watch the prince's face, and listen for what he does not say. Then in Chapter 17, someone comes to help. Stop at each question, think, and keep reading.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now show what you understood. Answer in full sentences, with details from the book. One, the prince makes no sound when he is whipped, just like Jemmy always did. What does that tell you? Two, what does Jemmy think about the prince afterward? Three, where does each outlaw go when the bear charges? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

cards.pluck: Pluck. There was a cast-iron streak of pluck in him. Pluck means courage, being brave when things are hard.
cards.defiant: Defiant. The prince remained defiant. I'm staying, he said. Defiant means refusing to give in.
cards.girded: Girded. Prince Brat only girded himself for the next blow. Girded means he got ready for something hard.
cards.snarling: Snarling. The bear came snarling down the embankment. Snarling means making a low, angry growl.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: Jemmy tells the outlaws, “Lay down the whip,” and calls them simpletons.
items.why: He speaks up to two outlaws to stop the whipping.

items.t: Billy whips the prince, and the prince does not make a sound.
items.why: He is hurt, but he stays strong.

items.t: When the bear charges, Cutwater drops the prince and runs off like a greyhound.
items.why: He runs to save himself and leaves the boy behind.
